# T2.02: which stage brings the MMU fault

`encode1 256 128 26` with `NVENC_VAR=stop=N` (each stage adds methods; the semaphore release is always last):

| stop | methods sent | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SET_OBJECT`, `SET_APPLICATION_ID` (H.264) | done in 0.03 ms, no error |
| 2 | + `SET_CONTROL_PARAMS` (H.264, CONSTQP, force out pic) | done, no error |
| 3 | + `SET_PICTURE_INDEX` and every buffer address (setup, status, bitstream, history, input, recon, coloc, 14 extra scratch buffers) | done, no error |
| 4 | + `EXECUTE` | timeout; error notifier status `0xffff`, info32 `0x1f` (MMU fault), info16 `0x1b` (NVENC0) |

The methods are accepted, and the fault comes from the engine's own memory accesses while it runs `EXECUTE`.
Moving buffers between system and video memory (`vid`, `allvid`) changes nothing, and neither does leaving out the 14
extra buffers (`NVENC_MINBUF=1`). So it's not a sysmem/vidmem placement issue or one of the optional buffers. The
next step (T2.03) is to get the faulting address.
